pullRequest.title: Stop the API saving panels that the editor would never build
pullRequest.body:
## Summary
Five chart rules that stop the API saving panels the editor never builds, one commit each. A second pass over the rules found them, and atrium doesn't catch any of them. They all need the report's recipe, so they're unknown (and pass) until porter passes it in. [sc-4821]

## Commits
- **Need a group-by on a table or map for a report that must be grouped.** A `GROUPED_ONLY` report could be saved ungrouped on a table or map, whose group-by is otherwise optional. Example: the `signups_by_plan` report.
- **Need a location dimension for a map.** The catalogue accepted a map for any report. The editor's chart picker now asks the new `map.needsLocation` rule instead of checking the dimensions itself.
- **Need the fields grouped and split by to be the report's dimensions.** Atrium only checks that a field exists in the recipe. While the field's type was unknown, the field-type rules passed too.
- **Refuse a field group-by on a date field.** The editor always groups by a date field as time. A field group-by groups by raw timestamps.
- **Check a time group-by against the main report.** The report must be a time series. Without a chosen date field, it mustn't be a `PICKED_AT_RUNTIME` report: atrium rejects those, which affects a dozen CRM reports.

## Notes
- The facts come from `factsFromKilnPanel`. Each is unknown when the dimension list or time field choice is missing.
- The rules apply to every catalogue chart, except the group-by one, which only applies to table and map. Number and gauge already refuse those reports.
- The editor's only change is the map check in the chart picker, and its behaviour is the same.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

nodes.body: I'm a little lost on these last two rules - it looks like we return `undefined` when the field or `report.dimensions` is `undefined`. I can't see what stops this applying to every report - even ones that don't use a `groupBy` or `splitBy`. We expect the values to be true, so is there a special case where an `undefined` fact means we skip the rule?
